The matrix $H$ is defined by entries $H_{ij} = \int_0^1 x^{i+j-2} dx = \frac{1}{i+j-1}$. This is the $n \times n$ Hilbert matrix.

Let the $j$-th entry of the last row of $H^{-1}$ be denoted by $a_j = (H^{-1})_{nj}$ for $1 \le j \le n$.
The relation $H^{-1} H = I$ implies that the dot product of the $n$-th row of $H^{-1}$ with the $j$-th column of $H$ is $\delta_{nj}$ (Kronecker delta). That is:
$$ \sum_{k=1}^n a_k H_{kj} = \delta_{nj} \quad \text{for } j=1, \dots, n $$
Substituting the integral form of $H_{kj}$:
$$ \sum_{k=1}^n a_k \int_0^1 x^{k+j-2} dx = \delta_{nj} $$
$$ \int_0^1 \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k x^{k-1} \right) x^{j-1} dx = \delta_{nj} $$
Let $P_{n-1}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k x^{k-1}$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n-1$. The condition becomes:
$$ \int_0^1 P_{n-1}(x) x^{j-1} dx = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } j=1, \dots, n-1 \\ 1 & \text{if } j=n \end{cases} $$
This characterizes $P_{n-1}(x)$ uniquely. Specifically, $P_{n-1}(x)$ must be orthogonal to all polynomials of degree less than $n-1$ on $[0,1]$, meaning $P_{n-1}(x)$ is proportional to the shifted Legendre polynomial of degree $n-1$, denoted $\mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x)$. The normalization condition $\int_0^1 P_{n-1}(x) x^{n-1} dx = 1$ fixes the proportionality constant.

The explicit coefficients of the shifted Legendre polynomial $\mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x)$ are given by:
$$ \mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^{n-k} \binom{n-1}{k-1} \binom{n+k-2}{k-1} x^{k-1} $$
(Note: using index $k$ for the power $x^{k-1}$, where $k$ runs from $1$ to $n$. Here, the binomial coefficient $\binom{n+k-2}{k-1}$ corresponds to $\binom{n+j-2}{j-1}$ when replacing $k$ with $j$.)

To determine the scaling factor $C$ such that $P_{n-1}(x) = C \mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x)$, we evaluate the integral condition for $j=n$:
$$ C \int_0^1 \mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x) x^{n-1} dx = 1 $$
Since $\mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x)$ is a linear combination of $1, \dots, x^{n-1}$, and is orthogonal to $1, \dots, x^{n-2}$, the integral is dominated by the leading term. The leading coefficient of $\mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x)$ (coefficient of $x^{n-1}$) is $\binom{2n-2}{n-1}$. It is a known property of shifted Legendre polynomials that:
$$ \int_0^1 \mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x) x^{n-1} dx = \frac{1}{(2n-1) \binom{2n-2}{n-1}} $$
Thus, the scaling factor is:
$$ C = (2n-1) \binom{2n-2}{n-1} $$
Multiplying the coefficients of $\mathcal{P}_{n-1}^*(x)$ by $C$ and adjusting for the sign convention ($(-1)^{n-k} = (-1)^{n+j}$ for the $j$-th term):
$$ (H^{-1})_{nj} = (-1)^{n+j} (2n-1) \binom{2n-2}{n-1} \binom{n-1}{j-1} \binom{n+j-2}{j-1} $$
This result can be numerically verified for small $n$. For example, for $n=3$, the entries are $30, -180, 180$. The formula yields these values correctly.
